meta.title: Operation of Trinocular Microscope in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To perform detailed microscopic examination of plant tissue sections, pollen, trichomes, and cellular structures with simultaneous viewing through eyepieces and camera port for documentation and teaching.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for histological examination of drug materials, photomicrography, and teaching demonstrations using the camera port.
procedure: Clean the stage, objectives, and eyepieces of the trinocular microscope with lens paper before use.
Connect the microscope to the power supply and switch on the halogen/LED illumination.
Set the light intensity to medium using the brightness control.
If a camera is attached to the trinocular port, connect it to the PC/monitor and open the imaging software.
Place the prepared slide (stained section or whole mount) on the mechanical stage and secure with the stage clips.
Start with the lowest power objective (4× or 10×) to locate the area of interest.
Adjust the coarse focus to bring the specimen into approximate focus, then use fine focus for sharp imaging.
Adjust the interpupillary distance so the two fields of view merge into one circular field.
Correct for individual eye differences using the diopter adjustment on the eyepieces.
For photomicrography: switch the light path to the camera port (trinocular prism); adjust exposure and white balance in the imaging software.
Progressively increase magnification (10×, 40×) as needed; use the mechanical stage controls to navigate the slide.
Adjust the condenser aperture diaphragm for optimal contrast at each magnification.
Capture and save images with appropriate file names including slide number, magnification, stain, and date.
After use, return to the lowest power objective, remove the slide, and clean the stage.
Clean all objectives gently with lens paper; cover the microscope with its dust cover.
Log usage in the equipment register.
precautions: Never allow the objective to touch the slide — approach from the side when focusing with high-power objectives.
Always start focusing with the lowest power objective — switching to high power without focusing on low power risks crashing the objective into the slide.
Clean objectives with lens paper only — regular tissue or cotton scratches the anti-reflection coating.
Keep the 100× oil-immersion objective clean — immediately remove immersion oil after use with lens paper and lens cleaning solvent.
Do not force the coarse focus knob when resistance is felt — this indicates the objective is close to the slide.
Handle slides with care — broken slides cause cuts and contamination.
Store the microscope covered and in a dry, dust-free area when not in use.
